chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Abu Basir, and Burayd, and al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them), said:

"In gold, for every forty mithqals, one mithqal; and in silver (dirhams), for every two hundred dirhams, five dirhams. And there is nothing (due) in less than forty mithqals, and nothing in less than two hundred dirhams. And there is nothing in the surplus (niyyif) until forty is completed, then there is one in it."

His saying (peace be upon him) 'and there is nothing in less than forty mithqals' allows for the meaning that he meant one dinar, because his word 'something' is ambiguous regarding the dinar, that which increases it, and that which decreases it, and it runs the course of the general statement that requires specification. And since we have narrated the detailed hadiths that in every twenty dinars, half a dinar is due, and in that which increases it, for every four dinars, one-tenth of a dinar is due, we interpret his saying (peace be upon him) 'and there is nothing in what is less than forty dinars' as meaning one dinar, because whenever it falls short of forty, only less than the dinar is due in it. As for his saying (peace be upon him) at the beginning of the report 'in every forty mithqals, one mithqal', there is no contradiction in it to what we said, because with us it is established that one dinar is due in it, even though this is not the first threshold of nisab. And if we interpret this report as we said, we have reconciled between these reports in a manner where there is no conflict between them.

key_terms.النَّيِّف: The surplus amount over a base number (e.g., 41-49)
key_terms.مِثْقَالٌ: A unit of weight for gold, equivalent to one dinar
key_terms.نِصَاب: The minimum threshold of wealth upon which khums or zakat becomes due

ai.seo_question: What is the khums rate and threshold for gold and silver in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific nisab (threshold) and rates for Zakat on gold (40 mithqals) and silver (200 dirhams), rather than Khums. It addresses the scholarly principle of *jam' bayn al-akhbar* (reconciling narrations), explaining how the phrase 'nothing is due in less than forty' is interpreted as referring to a single dinar rather than zero liability, thereby harmonizing it with other reports specifying fractional dues for amounts below the full threshold. This reflects the Usuli approach to resolving apparent textual contradictions in fiqh.
